"The search for Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, an Indian tourist who fell into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, has been halted due to safety concerns. The incident occurred on 23 August when the pavement beneath her suddenly gave way as she was walking along a road in the Malaysian capital.

***

Gali plunged approximately 8 metres (26 feet) into the sinkhole and vanished from sight. Despite extensive search efforts, rescuers have been unable to locate her, with only her slippers found as evidence of her presence at the site.

***

The rescue operation has employed a variety of resources and methods to try to find the missing woman. These include:

* Tracker dogs, remote cameras, ground-penetrating radar, high-pressure water jets, and excavators to clear debris from the underground drainage system.

***

By the eighth day of searching, which fell on Saturday, the country's fire and rescue department declared further diving operations too hazardous to continue. Dr Zaliha Mustafa, a minister in the prime minister's office, cited the safety and health of rescue personnel as primary reasons for suspending the mission. Two divers had attempted entry early Thursday but were withdrawn before reaching any obstacle.

***

Notably, authorities revealed that a soil slip had previously been reported at the very same location last year, raising questions about the area's stability and whether earlier warnings might have prevented this tragic event from occurring.

Is there anything else I can help with?"
